arxiv-2004-04545.title: C ​ P CP Properties of Higgs Boson Interactions with Top Quarks in the t ​ t ¯ ​ H t\bar{t}H and t ​ H tH Processes Using H → γ ​ γ H\rightarrow\gamma\gamma with the ATLAS Detector
arxiv-2004-04545.creator: The ATLAS Collaboration
arxiv-2004-04545.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by The ATLAS Collaboration. A study of the C ​ P CP properties of the interaction between the Higgs boson and top quarks is presented. Higgs bosons are identified via the diphoton decay channel ( H → γ ​ γ H\rightarrow\gamma\gamma ) and their production in association with a top quark pair ( t ​ t ¯ ​ H t\bar{t}H ) or single top quark ( t ​ H tH ) is studied.

arxiv-2010-01905.title: Information thermodynamics of financial markets: the Glosten-Milgrom model
arxiv-2010-01905.creator: Léo Touzo, Matteo Marsili, Don Zagier
arxiv-2010-01905.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Léo Touzo, Matteo Marsili, Don Zagier. The Glosten-Milgrom model describes a single asset market, where informed traders interact with a market maker, in the presence of noise traders. We derive an analogy between this financial model and a Szilárd information engine by i) showing that the optimal work extraction protocol in the latter coincides with the pricing strategy of the market maker in the former and ii) defining a market analogue of the physical temperature from the analysis of the distribution of market orders.

arxiv-2205-09952.title: The Dependence of Stellar Activity Cycles on Effective Temperature
arxiv-2205-09952.creator: Leonid Kitchatinov
arxiv-2205-09952.description: Abstract This paper proposes the idea that the observed dependence of stellar activity cycles on rotation rate can be a manifestation of a stronger dependence on the effective temperature. Observational evidence is recalled and theoretical arguments are given for the presence of cyclic activity in the case of sufficiently slow rotation only.

arxiv-2308-14477.title: Medical needle tip tracking based on Optical Imaging and AI
arxiv-2308-14477.creator: Zhuoqi Cheng, Simon Lyck Bjært Sørensen, Mikkel Werge Olsen, Rene Lynge Eriksen, Thiusius R. Savarimuthu
arxiv-2308-14477.description: Abstract \IEEEoverridecommandlockouts \overrideIEEEmargins INTRODUCTION Medical needle tip tracking plays an important role in various needle-based procedures such as biopsy, tumor ablation, intravenous access and deep brain stimulation. Accurate and real-time tracking of the needle tip assures precise targeting, minimizing tissue damage and enhance procedural efficiency.

arxiv-2310-15569.title: MuLMS: A Multi-Layer Annotated Text Corpus for Information Extraction in the Materials Science Domain
arxiv-2310-15569.creator: Timo Pierre Schrader Matteo Finco Stefan Grünewald, Felix Hildebrand Annemarie Friedrich
arxiv-2310-15569.description: Abstract Keeping track of all relevant recent publications and experimental results for a research area is a challenging task. Prior work has demonstrated the efficacy of information extraction models in various scientific areas. Recently, several datasets have been released for the yet understudied materials science domain.

arxiv-2410-03604.title: Koszul duality and Calabi-Yau structures
arxiv-2410-03604.creator: Julian Holstein, Manuel Rivera
arxiv-2410-03604.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Julian Holstein, Manuel Rivera. We show that Koszul duality between differential graded categories and pointed curved coalgebras interchanges smooth and proper Calabi-Yau structures. This result is a generalization and conceptual explanation of the following two applications. For a finite-dimensional Lie algebra a smooth Calabi-Yau structure on the universal enveloping algebra is equivalent to a proper Calabi-Yau structure on the Chevalley-Eilenberg chain coalgebra, which exists if and only if Poincaré duality is satisfied.

arxiv-2504-21400.title: Who Gets the Callback? Generative AI and Gender Bias Thanks: Both authors contributed equally to this work.
arxiv-2504-21400.creator: Sugat Chaturvedi, Rochana Chaturvedi
arxiv-2504-21400.description: Abstract Generative artificial intelligence (AI)—particularly large language models (LLMs)—is being rapidly deployed in recruitment and for candidate shortlisting. We audit several mid-sized open-source LLMs for gender bias using a dataset of 332,044 332,044 real-world online job postings. For each posting, we prompt the model to recommend whether an equally qualified male or female candidate should receive an interview callback.

arxiv-2510-06570.title: Topological Hall Effect in PrSb 2
arxiv-2510-06570.creator: Shingo Araki 1,2, Hinata Izumida 2, Kazuto Akiba 1,2, Tatsuo C. Kobayashi 1,2, Takashi Kambe 1,2
arxiv-2510-06570.description: Abstract PrSb 2 exhibits a charge-density wave (CDW) transition at T CDW = 100 T_{\mathrm{CDW}}=100 K and antiferromagnetic (AFM) ordering at T N = 5 T_{\mathrm{N}}=5 K at ambient pressure. Hall resistivity measurements revealed an anomalous feature within the AFM state, which was attributed to the topological Hall effect (THE), ruling out contributions from the ordinary and anomalous Hall effects.

pmc-12470845.title: The Structural and Functional Diversities of Bacteria Inhabiting Plant Woody Tissues and Their Interactions with Fungi
pmc-12470845.creator: Rana Haidar, Amira Yacoub, Ouiza Mesguida, Rémy Guyoneaud, Eléonore Attard, Patrice Rey, Zonghua Wang
pmc-12470845.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). In recent studies, the bacterial and fungal communities associated with plant wood have received considerable attention. Due to microorganisms’ vertical migration from roots to leaves, these communities provide critical links between the rhizosphere and phyllosphere microbiome. Recent investigations have shown that anatomical and chemical wood characteristics shape the microbiota inhabiting living or dead wood tissues, leading to variation in the observed decomposition of these materials.

pmc-12671307.title: Virtual Humans in Virtual Reality Mental Health Research: Systematic Review
pmc-12671307.creator: Shu Wei, Daniel Freeman, Aitor Rovira, Andrew Coristine
pmc-12671307.description: BackgroundVirtual reality (VR) is showing increasing promise for assessing, understanding, and treating mental health difficulties. Virtual humans (VHs) represent a key aspect within many VR mental health applications. While VHs can play diverse roles and display varied characteristics, their design and influence have rarely been the primary focus of mental health research.

pmc-12751575.title: Unmet need for healthcare services among unemployed people – findings from a national survey in Finland
pmc-12751575.creator: Hanna Rinne, Ari-Pekka Sihvonen, Visa Väisänen, Lars Leemann, Anna-Mari Aalto
pmc-12751575.description: BackgroundUnemployed people have higher morbidity compared to employed people. Both the frequent use and the underutilization of healthcare services are common among unemployed people, potentially leading to unmet healthcare needs. We studied the differences in self-reported no need and unmet need for healthcare services between unemployed and employed persons and the health-related factors associated with these differences.

pmc-13212877.title: Mitigation of microbial biocontamination in cyanobacterial ethanol synthesis via alginate encapsulation
pmc-13212877.creator: Xiangxiao Liu, Xiang Liu, Yanfei Pan, Huili Sun, Bo Liang, Jiahui Sun, Tianzhong Liu, Guodong Luan, Xuefeng Lu
pmc-13212877.description: BackgroundSustainable biofuels have spurred interest in cyanobacterial ethanol production, yet large-scale application is severely hindered by microbial contamination—a devastating challenge that lacks universally effective, biocompatible mitigation strategies. Traditional methods such as pH manipulation or antibiotic application are often physiologically incompatible, environmentally unsustainable, or ineffective against diverse contaminant consortia.

pmc-13500202.title: The Right to Food for Children With Cerebral Palsy in South Africa: Examining Nutritional Access and Structural Barriers
pmc-13500202.creator: Tiya Vala, Radia Ameen, Skye Nandi Adams
pmc-13500202.description: BackgroundChildren with cerebral palsy (CP) are at increased risk of malnutrition due to feeding difficulties, higher nutritional requirements and the additional caregiving demands associated with disability. Households caring for children with CP may therefore experience greater vulnerability to food insecurity, particularly in low‐resource contexts.

pmc-13661808.title: How to Break Through the Ceiling of Scientific Progress?—Innovation Challenges and Pathways Based on the Fitness Landscape Framework
pmc-13661808.creator: Kunjie Zhu, Li Sun, Peng Du
pmc-13661808.description: Science has not hit an absolute ceiling; it is stranded on a local peak. Viewed through Wright's fitness landscape, today's evaluation and funding systems over‐select, refining work within established paradigms while suppressing the drift and recombination needed to cross fitness valleys. Restoring room for non‐consensus, curiosity‐driven and interdisciplinary research is an institutional task as much as an intellectual one.
